content.comment_body: The specified range for the [product_name] analog module is -50 to 200°C. However, in practice, the display shows -50°C for a short circuit (as expected) and 177°C when the circuit is open, instead of the anticipated 200°C. Why does this happen? How can I ensure the system displays 200°C? Thank you.
Hello [user_name], You may find more details by searching for "[product_name] °C precision". This should assist you in connecting your sensors properly. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], I appreciate your suggestion, but it doesn't address my issue. My concern is that [product_name] shows 177°C instead of 200°C when the sensor connection is left open or when the measurement exceeds the range. In testing, heating the sensor normally displayed temperatures up to 200°C, but going beyond that resulted in a display of 177°C. The same occurs with an open sensor connection—177°C is shown. I hadn't realized the system outputs 177°C rather than 200°C for over-range input. I'm satisfied with the explanation now. Thanks again. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users discovered that with the [product_name] analog module, the system returns 177°C when the measured temperature exceeds the module's range or when the sensor is disconnected, instead of displaying the expected maximum value of 200°C. Measurements within range (up to 200°C) are shown accurately, but above that threshold or with an open circuit, the display defaults to 177°C, leading to confusion regarding how the system signals over-range or fault conditions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that the system should display 200°C when the sensor is over-ranged or disconnected, rather than the value 177°C currently shown.
